paragraphs: Rav Chisda (the priest)
(In the Jerusalem Talmud he is sometimes called Chisdai, Chisdi, or Chisdiyy.)[^1]

This great man, who attained Torah, greatness, and length of days, and occupied the seat of Rav and Rav Huna in Sura—nothing at all is known to us about who his forefathers or family were; he is known only by the name “Rav Chisda.”

As for what we find in [Sanhedrin 8a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.8a.10-11)[^13], where Rav Nachman bar Yaakov said to Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda, “Thus your father’s father said in the name of Rav,” referring to Rav Chanan bar Rava: Hyman calls this a scribal error there and says it should read “your mother’s father,” as we shall explain below.

When Rav founded his great academy in Sura, Rav Chisda was then two years old. This is explicit in the Epistle of R.Sh.G. [רש״ג], part III, beginning of chapter 2: Rav came to Babylonia in the year 530 of the era of contracts, and Rav Chisda died in 620 of that era, having lived ninety-two years; Rav presided for twenty-eight years. Thus Rav Chisda was two when Rav came to Babylonia and thirty when Rav died. Therefore, without doubt, he still had the privilege of receiving Rav’s teaching from his own mouth.[^2]

This accounts for what we find in [Sukkah 33a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.33a.16)[^14], [Bekhorot 45a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.45a.10), and Niddah 49a[^15]: Rav Chisda said, “Our great teacher (Rav) said this; may the Omnipresent be his help.” Likewise, [Berakhot 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.38b.4) has “Rav Chisda expounded in the name of our teacher—and who is that? Rav.” In [Beitzah 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.25a.3)[^16], Rav Chisda said, “From the words of our teacher we shall learn.” (Rashi explains that Rav Huna, Rav Chisda, and Rav Nachman were all students of Rav.) In [Yevamot 110b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.110b.15), Rav Chisda explicitly speaks in Rav’s name.

We also find “Rav Chisda said in the name of Rav” in [Berakhot 43a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.43a.14)[^18], [Eruvin 97a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.97a.7), Pesachim 106a[^17], [Nazir 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.43b.1), [Avodah Zarah 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.31a.7), [52a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.52a.13), and [60b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.60b.10)[^19], and [Menachot 17a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.17a.5-7). Rav’s teachings were so dear to him that he said in [Shabbat 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.10b.6), “Anyone who comes and tells me a new teaching of Rav’s—I shall give him two gifts from an ox” (for he was a priest).

We likewise find in [Shabbat 144b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.144b.12) that Rav Chisda said, “From the words of our teacher (Shmuel) we shall learn.” Hyman says he found no face-to-face exchange with Rav or Shmuel and takes this as a sign that Chisda was not counted among Rav’s students.[^20]

Hyman identifies Avimi as Rav Chisda’s principal teacher, citing Rav Chisda’s remark in [Arakhin 22a](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.22a.4): “I took good blows from Avimi.”[^21] In [Avodah Zarah 14b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.14b.6-7) he put a difficulty to Avimi because he had not understood the interpretation of the Mishnah, and Avimi explained it to him.

Rav Chisda also speaks in Avimi’s name in [Sukkah 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.16b.9), [Ketubot 71b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.71b.7) and [100b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.100b.15), [Gittin 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.26b.4), [Sotah 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.9a.14), [Bava Kamma 13b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.13b.18), [Sanhedrin 15a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.15a.2) and [81b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.81b.15), and [Zevachim 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.26a.4)[^22]. Hyman also lists Zevachim 27a, [Menachot 77a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.77a.3), and [Bekhorot 44a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.44a.21)[^23]. [Menachot 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.7a.7-9) asks: “Did Avimi teach Menachot in Rav Chisda’s school? But Rav Chisda said, ‘I took good blows from Avimi’!” It answers that Avimi had forgotten the tractate and came to Rav Chisda so that he would remind him of his learning.

He also received teaching from all the great students of Rav and Shmuel. Rav Chisda speaks in the name of Rav Yirmeya bar Abba (a student and colleague of Rav) in [Berakhot 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.55b.5), [Taanit 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.12b.12), and [Sanhedrin 103a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.103a.11-13). Hyman also cites Zevachim 25b[^24] and proposes reading the same attribution in [Horayot 6a](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.6a.11)[^25].

Rav Chisda also speaks in the name of Mar Ukva, whom Hyman describes as Shmuel’s student and a resident of Kafri. The attribution appears in [Berakhot 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.10b.33-35) and [29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.29b.10), [Shabbat 116b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.116b.9), [Eruvin 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.21b.24), [Pesachim 40a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.40a.6), [Ketubot 48a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.48a.5-6) and [70a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.70a.2), [Gittin 88a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.88a.20-21), and [Avodah Zarah 17a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.17a.7) and [27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.27a.19).[^26] It also appears in [Niddah 52a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.52a.19).[^27] In [Sanhedrin 70a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.70a.21), Rav Chisda speaks in the name of Rav Ukva. Hyman also records a reading with Mar Ukva.[^28] In [Sotah 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.39a.6), Rav Chisda called on Mar Ukva, and an exposition followed.[^29] In [Yevamot 63b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.63b.7), Rav Chisda speaks in the name of Mar Ukva bar Chiyya.[^30]

Rav Chisda also speaks in the name of Zeiri in alternate readings in [Berakhot 43a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.43a.14) and [Sanhedrin 69b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.69b.6), and in [Avodah Zarah 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.31a.7) and [49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.49b.6). At 31a, Rav Chisda reports what Abba bar Chama told him in Zeiri’s name. Hyman considers the reading “Abba bar Rav Chisda” in the parallel an error.[^31]
Rav Chisda speaks in the name of Rav Chama bar Gurya in [Menachot 78a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.78a.7).

In [Chullin 63a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.63a.17-18), Rav Chisda cites Rav Chanan bar Rava, whom Hyman identifies as Rav’s son-in-law and Rav Chisda’s father-in-law. In [Pesachim 117a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.117a.21-22), Rav Chisda recalls the Psalms text at the school of Rav Chanin bar Rav. Hyman proposes reading “bar Rava” there on the authority of Dikdukei Soferim.[^32]

Rav Chisda speaks in Rabbi Yochanan’s name in [Pesachim 117a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.117a.1), [Yevamot 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.25b.10), and [Makkot 23a](https://www.sefaria.org/Makkot.23a.9), and in an alternate reading in [Avodah Zarah 27b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.27b.2). Hyman also cites [Berakhot 58b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.58b.2-4) as a transmission in Rabbi Yochanan’s name.[^33] Yet Hyman finds no record of Rav Chisda going to the Land of Israel in Rabbi Yochanan’s lifetime. In [Berakhot 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.24b.13-14), Rav Huna speaks in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, and Rav Chisda replies, “By God, even if Rabbi Yochanan told it to me with his own mouth, I would not heed him.”[^34] Hyman takes this to imply that Rav Chisda was not Rabbi Yochanan’s student.

Hyman concludes that Rav Chisda received Rabbi Yochanan’s teachings from travellers who came down from the Land of Israel. In [the end of Jerusalem Talmud, Rosh Hashanah 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Rosh_Hashanah.4.10.5), Rav Chisda tells Rabbi Ze’ira of those “who come down from the West and report there in the name of Rabbi Yochanan.” Hyman suggests that this explains why Rav Chisda calls Ulla, one of those travellers, “our teachers who come down” in [Berakhot 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.38b.4). In [Pesachim 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.33b.2-4), Rav Acha bar Rav Avya quotes Rabbi Yochanan, and Rav Chisda replies, “Who heeds you and Rabbi Yochanan, your teacher?”

Rav Chisda speaks in the name of Rabbi Yonatan in [Bava Kamma 67a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.67a.9-12). Hyman gives “Rabbi Yochanan” as the corrected reading. Rav Chisda speaks in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak in [Sukkah 44b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.44b.3) and [Chullin 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.16b.9).[^35] He asks Rav Yitzchak questions in [Berakhot 27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.27a.13) and [43a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.43a.17).

Rav Chisda speaks in the name of Ravina bar Shila in [Sukkah 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.13a.4-6), [Moed Katan 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.17b.7), and [Yevamot 68b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.68b.3). Hyman includes [Zevachim 36b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.36b.8), where he proposes reading Shila for Sila, and cites Dikdukei Soferim for reading Ravina bar Shila in place of Rav Shila in Moed Katan.[^36] In [Ketubot 75a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.75a.12), Rav Chisda says, “I heard this matter from a great man—and who is that? Rabbi Shila.” Hyman proposes Ravina bar Shila because Rabbi Shila died before Rav began to preside. He suggests that the mark in “Ravi’” [רבי׳] and the word “bar” fell out.[^37]

Rav Chisda speaks in the name of Rav Katina in [Bava Metzia 79a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.79a.12), [Bekhorot 35a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.35a.6), and [Arakhin 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.32a.8). Hyman also says Rav Chisda received teaching from Rav Hamnuna, a student of Rav. Rav Chisda raises a difficulty with him in [Jerusalem Talmud, Horayot 3:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Horayot.3.2.17), and in [Shabbat 97a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.97a.11) Rav Yosef reports that Rav Hamnuna resolved a question of Rav Chisda’s.[^38]

When Rav Huna began to preside in Sura, Rav Chisda studied before him and became his student and colleague. Hyman puts Rav Chisda at about forty years of age at the time and dates Rav Huna’s death to 608 of the era of contracts, after forty years as head of the academy. Rav Chisda raises objections to Rav Huna in [Berakhot 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.24b.13) and [Pesachim 73a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.73a.14). In [Pesachim 101b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.101b.2), he speaks in Rav Huna’s name, and in [Beitzah 17a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.17a.1), Rava transmits the teaching through him from Rav Huna. At Rav Huna’s funeral in [Moed Katan 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25a.10-11), Rav Chisda explicitly says that he learned these rulings from him.

In [Pesachim 107a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.107a.5-6), “Rav Huna asked Rav Chisda” is a printing error according to Hyman, who reads the question in the opposite direction.[^39] In [Bava Metzia 33a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.33a.15), Rav Chisda asks Rav Huna about a student whose teacher needs him. Rav Huna suspects that Rav Chisda means himself, takes offense, and says, “Chisda, Chisda! I do not need you. You need me.” They were displeased with each other and stopped visiting. Hyman takes this to have lasted forty years. Afterwards Rav Chisda observed forty fasts for having distressed Rav Huna, and Rav Huna observed forty fasts for having suspected Rav Chisda.[^8]

Rav Chisda was careful to leave rulings in Rav Huna’s jurisdiction to him. In [Eruvin 62b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.62b.11-12), the Gemara says that they asked Rav Chisda questions throughout Rav Huna’s years, and he refrained from ruling there. In [Bava Metzia 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.7a.4), “The incident was in Rav Chisda’s school, and Rav Chisda was in Rav Huna’s school.” [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Bava_Metzia.7a.4.1) explains that they came before Rav Chisda, who brought the case to Rav Huna.

Rav Huna held him in high regard. In [Gittin 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.7a.13-16), the exilarch asks Rav Huna for the source of the ban on a groom’s crown. Rav Huna calls it a rabbinic decree. When he rises to relieve himself, Rav Chisda says, “A verse is written.” Rav Huna returns to find them discussing it and says, “By God, it is rabbinic! But Chisda is your name, and gracious are your words.” In [Jerusalem Talmud, Sotah 9:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.9.15.7), the exilarch sends the question to Rav Chisdai, and Rabbi Yochanan hears his answer and says, “He is gracious, and his words are gracious.”[^40]

In [Shabbat 82a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.82a.2), Rav Huna asks his son Rabbah, “Why don’t you study with Rav Chisda? His teachings are sharp.” Hyman takes this as evidence that Rav Chisda was Rav Huna’s student and colleague, as [Tosafot on Yevamot 83b, s.v. Amrei bei Rav](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Yevamot.83b.5.1) also says. In [Gittin 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.31b.10), Rav Huna and Rav Chisda are sitting together when Geniva passes. One says, “Let us stand before him,” and the other replies, “Should we stand before a contentious man?” Meanwhile Geniva comes over to them.

Hyman thinks it very plausible that Rav Chisda went to Kafri and ruled there during the years of their estrangement. [Eruvin 62b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.62b.13) says that Rav Chisda ruled in Kafri during Rav Huna’s lifetime. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Eruvin.62b.13.1) explains that Kafri lay outside Rav Huna’s jurisdiction and that both places lay in Babylonia. Rashi names Pumbedita as Rav Huna’s seat, and Hyman proposes reading Sura. In [Bava Metzia 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.6b.1), Rav Hoshaya tells Rabbah, “When you go before Rav Chisda in Kafri, ask him.” Hyman considers it more likely that Kafri was Rav Chisda’s permanent home. There he received much teaching from Mar Ukva, whom [Kiddushin 44b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.44b.7) places in Kafri with his court. In Hyman’s reconstruction, Rav Chisda would go to Sura to study with Rav Huna, then return home and issue rulings there.

Disputes between Rav Huna and Rav Chisda occur in [Berakhot 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.25a.3-5), [Shabbat 146a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.146a.10), [Sukkah 3b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.3b.11), [Beitzah 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.14a.4-5), [Ketubot 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.24b.9) and [50a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.50a.13), [Gittin 64a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.64a.2-3), [Bava Batra 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.31b.2-4), and [Chullin 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.10a.6-7).[^41]

Rav Chisda was present when Rav Huna died, according to Hyman. In [Moed Katan 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25a.9-15), Rav Chisda objects when they propose placing a Torah scroll on Rav Huna’s bier. He then recalls what he learned from Rav Huna about carrying out a scholar on his original bier through the doorway. Rabbi Abba eulogizes Rav Huna, saying that he was worthy of the Divine Presence resting upon him, but Babylonia prevented it. Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda objects, and his father taps him with his sandal. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Moed_Katan.25a.14.1) identifies his father as Rav Chisda.[^42] The account goes on to describe the transfer of Rav Huna’s coffin to the Land of Israel. Hyman infers that Rav Chisda went with it.

Hyman uses this visit to explain [Yevamot 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.21b.2), where Rav Chisda says, “I heard this matter from a great man—and who was that? Rabbi Ami.” Hyman takes Rabbi Ami to have succeeded Rabbi Yochanan as head of the academy by the time of this brief visit, and suggests that this accounts for the description.[^43] In [Eruvin 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.38b.8), when Rav Huna dies, Rav Chisda enters to set one statement of Rav against another.

Hyman finds no instance of Rav Chisda reporting in Rav Yehudah’s name or speaking with him. In [Berakhot 43a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.43a.17), Rav Chisda tells Rav Yitzchak, “Rav Yehudah is different, for the Land of Israel is dear to him.” In [Chullin 110b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.110b.3), Rami bar Tamri tells Rav Chisda, “Had you been in Rav Yehudah’s place, I would have shown you my sharpness.”[^44] Hyman takes this to imply that Rav Chisda had never been in Rav Yehudah’s place.

His leading colleagues included Rav Nachman, Rav Sheshet, and Rabbah bar Rav Huna. In [Eruvin 67a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.67a.4), when Rav Chisda met Rav Sheshet, his lips trembled at Rav Sheshet’s Mishnayot. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Eruvin.67a.4.1) explains that they were well ordered in Rav Sheshet’s memory and that Rav Chisda feared being asked to reconcile contradictory Mishnayot. Rav Sheshet’s whole body trembled at Rav Chisda’s dialectical sharpness. In [Berakhot 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.49a.15), Rav Chisda recalls, “I came to the exilarch’s house and recited Grace after Meals, and Rav Sheshet stiffened his neck at me like a snake.”

In [Berakhot 47b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.47b.20), Rabbi Ami says that two Torah scholars who sharpen each other in halakhah may count together for a zimmun. Rav Chisda points to himself and Rav Sheshet as the example, and Rav Sheshet points to himself and Rav Chisda. They address each other as Mar in [Gittin 68a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.68a.4) and travel together in [Berakhot 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.30a.2-3). Rav Chisda asks Rav Sheshet a question in [Berakhot 33a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.33a.36-37).[^3] Hyman cites Eruvin 22a for their disagreements.[^45]

When Rav Chisda came to study with Rav Huna, he grew close to his teacher’s son, and the two studied together. Rav Chisda and Rabbah bar Rav Huna give joint rulings in [Pesachim 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.10b.15), [Ketubot 99b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.99b.7), and [Niddah 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.28a.6). Hyman also cites Shabbat 83a.[^46] Both regularly visited the exilarch’s house, as in [Sukkah 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.10b.5) and [26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.26a.3), and travelled together by boat in [Chullin 105b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.105b.14).

At first Rabbah was reluctant to study with Rav Chisda. In [Shabbat 82a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.82a.2), he asks his father Rav Huna, “Why should I go to him? When I do, he occupies me with worldly matters. He tells me that one who enters a privy should sit down slowly and avoid straining. The rectum rests on three ‘teeth,’ and if they come loose, the person could be in danger.” Rav Huna replies, “He is concerned with people’s lives, and you call that worldly matters? All the more reason to go to him!” Hyman observes that the two appear studying together regularly after this.

When Rav Nachman came to Sura, Rav Chisda and Rabbah bar Rav Huna went to see him, as recounted in [Sukkah 14b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.14b.11-12), [Ketubot 99b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.99b.8), and [Shevuot 48b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.48b.4). In [Bava Batra 132b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.132b.7), Rav Nachman visits Rav Chisda, who asks him about a marriage settlement. In [Shabbat 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.10a.5), Rav Chisda and Rabbah sit in judgment all day and grow faint. Rav Chiyya bar Rav of Difti teaches them, “Any judge who renders a judgment in its perfect truth, even for a single hour,” and so on.[^47]

Rav Nachman, Rav Chisda, and Rav Sheshet also appear together at the exilarch’s house in [Eruvin 39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.39b.7-8). Rav Nachman and Rav Chisda give joint rulings in [Bava Metzia 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.10a.5) and [Menachot 81b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.81b.16-17).[^48] In [Bava Kamma 27b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.27b.10-11), Rav Nachman sends Rav Chisda the reply, “Chisda, Chisda! Are you collecting fines in Babylonia?” Rav Chisda also speaks with Rav Chananel in [Megillah 18b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.18b.15). See the [Rav Chananel entry](https://www.girsology.com/toledot.html?entry=h-ca67ac911a81d315&lang=he).

Ulla was also his colleague. In [Berakhot 58b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.58b.2-4), they are travelling together when they reach the doorway of Rav Chana bar Chanilai’s house, and Rav Chisda sighs. In [Taanit 4b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.4b.4-5), Ulla says that Rav Chisda’s teaching is “like vinegar to the teeth.” In [Berakhot 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.38b.4), the Talmud identifies Ulla among “our teachers who come down” from the Land of Israel, quoting Rabbi Yochanan. Hyman understands this title as a reference to Ulla’s bringing teachings from the Land of Israel to Babylonia.

Rav Chisda also disputes with Rav Natan bar Oshaya in [Yevamot 89a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.89a.6-7) and [Chullin 138a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.138a.10-11).[^49] In [Zevachim 36b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.36b.10), Rav Chisda quotes a teaching that Rav Dimi bar Chinana was fond of repeating.

Rav Chisda reports an exposition by Mari bar Mar in [Eruvin 21a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.21a.13), and in an alternate reading in [Sanhedrin 38a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.38a.4).[^11] Hyman also cites the parallel in [Gittin 88a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.88a.20-21) and flags a scribal error there.[^50] Rav Chisda and Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi give differing opinions in [Sanhedrin 56b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.56b.10), [96b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.96b.1), and [100a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.100a.11), and in [Menachot 93a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.93a.15-16) and [98a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.98a.10). They also debate the healing leaf in [another passage on 98a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.98a.13-14). [Tosafot on Menachot 93a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Menachot.93a.15.1) describes them as colleagues and distinguishes this Rav Yitzchak from an earlier sage of the same name.

Rav Chisda also disputes with Rabbi Avina in [Ketubot 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.24b.13). [Shabbat 82a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.82a.5) names Ravina alongside Rav Chisda. Hyman proposes reading Rabbi Avina there. In an alternate version in [Berakhot 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.24b.14), Rabbah bar bar Chana quotes Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, and Rav Chisda objects.

His rulings appear throughout the Babylonian and Jerusalem Talmuds. In the Jerusalem Talmud he is sometimes called Rav Chisdai or Chisdi. Hyman compares the statement in [Jerusalem Talmud Megillah](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.1.6.2) that Rav Chisdi assigns the ruling to Rabbi Yehudah with the parallel in [Beitzah 28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.28b.5).[^12] The story of the exilarch asking Chisdai about the crown appears in [Jerusalem Talmud, Sotah 9:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.9.15.7) and [Ruth Rabbah 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Ruth_Rabbah.3.1), with a Babylonian parallel in [Gittin 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.7a.13-16).[^51] In [Sanhedrin 1:2:30](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.1.2.30), Rabbi Zeira reports a teaching in the name of Rav Chisdai. The related passages in [Sheviit 10:1:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sheviit.10.1.11) and [Rosh Hashanah 3:1:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Rosh_Hashanah.3.1.5) spell his name Chisda.[^52] In [Eruvin 1:6:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.1.6.3), Abba bar Rav Chuna responds to Rav Chisdai. Hyman identifies Abba with Rabbah bar Rav Huna.[^2]
His students and those who transmit his sayings:
R’ Ada bar Rav Yitzchak reports Rav Chisda at the end of Menachot.[^4]

Abaye raised a difficulty to Rav Chisda in [Taanit 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.12a.1).[^53] In [Zevachim 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.14a.19), Abaye asked Rav Chisda’s interpreter to ask his master whether a non-priest may carry the sacrificial blood. In [Yoma 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.49a.2-3), Rav Sheshet puts the same question through Rav Chisda’s interpreter. Rabbi Evyatar sent a ruling to Rav Chisda from the Land of Israel in [Gittin 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.6b.6).

Rav Oshaya and Rav Chananya lived in Rav Chisda’s time, as in [Bava Metzia 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.6b.1). Rav Chisda sent halakhic questions to Rabbah through Rav Acha bar Rav Huna, whom Hyman calls his student, in [Pesachim 47a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.47a.8) and [Yevamot 89b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.89b.7).

Hyman cites Bava Metzia 86a for an exchange between Rav Acha bar Yosef and Rav Chisda.[^54] In [Chullin 105a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.105a.7), Rav Acha bar Yosef asks Rav Chisda about meat caught between the teeth. In [Pesachim 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.33b.2-4), Rav Acha bar Rav Avya teaches in the name of Rabbi Yochanan before Rav Chisda, who asks, “Who will listen to you and to Rabbi Yochanan, your teacher?”[^55]

Rav Acha bar Ulla sat before Rav Chisda in [Shabbat 54b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.54b.11). Rav Achadvoi bar Ami raised a contradiction before Rav Chisda in [Pesachim 75a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.75a.8-9).

Rav Idi reported a teaching in the name of Rav Chisda before Rabbi Yosi, near the end of [Jerusalem Talmud, Yevamot 11:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.11.2.8).[^56] Rav Idi bar Avin sat before Rav Chisda in [Pesachim 101b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.101b.2-3). He cites Rav Chisda in [Eruvin 59b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.59b.9) and [Bava Metzia 4a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.4a.8). In [Bava Batra 33a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.33a.4-5), Rav Chisda said of him, “Is this the man of whom they say that he is a great man?” and addressed him as Mar.[^57]

Rabbi Ba reports a teaching in the name of Rav Chisda in [Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat 7:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.7.1.9-10). A Galilean expounded before Rav Chisda in [Shabbat 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.31b.10) (continuing on [32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.32a.1)), [Bava Kamma 52a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.52a.5), [Sanhedrin 113a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.113a.15), and [Makkot 23a](https://www.sefaria.org/Makkot.23a.6).

Rav Huna bar Chinana sat before Rav Chisda in [Moed Katan 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.9b.11). In [Moed Katan 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.16a.12), he gives a ruling in Rav Chisda’s name. Mar Zutra taught in Rav Chisda’s name in [Chullin 44b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.44b.11).

Rabbi Zeira said to Rav Chisda, “Let the master come and teach,” in [Berakhot 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.49a.15). Rabbi Zeira cites Rav Chisda in [Beitzah 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.33b.5), [Ketubot 95a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.95a.6), and Sotah [39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.39a.2), [39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.39b.4-5), and [43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.43b.5). In the Jerusalem Talmud, Rabbi Zeira reports teachings in Rav Chisda’s name in [Sheviit 10:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sheviit.10.1.11), [Shabbat 7:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.7.1.7-8), [Eruvin 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.1.1.25) and [5:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.5.7.6), [Rosh Hashanah 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Rosh_Hashanah.3.1.5), [Megillah 1:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.1.9.6), and [Nedarim 6:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.6.8.10).[^58] Hyman says his name should also be read in [Berakhot 9:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.9.2.6) and in Sanhedrin 1:4.[^59]

Rabbi Chizkiyah taught in Rav Chisda’s name in [Jerusalem Talmud, Shekalim 4:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shekalim.4.4.5). Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin asked Rav Chisda a question in [Menachot 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.49a.20). He reports an incident in Rav Chisda’s study hall in [Kiddushin 50a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.50a.6) and in [Bava Metzia 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.7a.4). Rav Chiyya bar Ashi transmitted a teaching in Rav Chisda’s name in [Sanhedrin 43a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.43a.10).[^60]

Rav Chiyya, son of Rabbah bar Nachmani, cites Rav Chisda in [Berakhot 43a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.43a.14), according to the reading Hyman attributes to Dikdukei Soferim, and in [Sanhedrin 69b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.69b.6) and [Avodah Zarah 49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.49b.6). Hyman considers “the son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Nachmani” in [Avodah Zarah 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.31a.7) a scribal error.[^61] Rav Chiyya, son of Rav Natan, transmitted Rav Chisda’s teaching in [Pesachim 41a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.41a.21).[^62]

Rav Chama asked Rav Chisda about Rav’s statement in [Nazir 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.20a.7). Rav Chanan bar Chisda objected to Rav Chisda’s ruling in [Shabbat 48a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.48a.9). Hyman takes him to have been Rav Chisda’s son, citing [Moed Katan 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25a.13).[^63]

Rav Chinana reports a teaching in Rav Chisda’s name near the beginning of [Jerusalem Talmud, Maaserot 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maasrot.1.1.5). At the end of [Jerusalem Talmud, Eruvin 4:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.4.10.2), Rabbi Acha reports in Rabbi Chinana’s name, and Rav Chisdai gives the same ruling. Rav Chinana Vardan objected to Rav Chisda’s words, and Rav Chisda said, “Vardan has fallen silent,” in [Gittin 64b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.64b.10-14).

Rav Chanina, whom Hyman calls “of Chozai,” came before Rav Chisda in [Moed Katan 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.20a.14) after receiving news of his father’s death from Bei Chozai. Rabbi Tavi cites Rav Chisda in [Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat 3:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.3.7.11).[^64] Rabbi Yose bar Bun also cites him near the end of [Jerusalem Talmud, Ketubot 8:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Ketubot.8.11.2).

Rav Yosef addressed Rav Chisda as Mar in [Kiddushin 59b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.59b.14). Hyman gives another instance at Shabbat 96b.[^65] Rav Chisda asked Rav Yosef, “Have you heard this from Rav Yehudah?” in [Ketubot 53b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.53b.5).

In [Eruvin 40b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.40b.16), the Sages sent Rav Yeimar the Elder to Rav Chisda on the eve of Rosh Hashanah. Hyman reports that the She’iltot gives his name as Rabbi Yeiva the Elder. Rav Chisda greeted him with a proverb: “When someone lifts a damp log, he wants the spot it was lying on.”

Rabbi Yaakov cites Rav Chisda in [Berakhot 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.29b.16) and [Ketubot 80a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.80a.4).[^66] Yaakov of Hadeyyav asked Rav Chisda a question in [Bava Batra 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.26b.2).

Rav Yitzchak bar Ami cites Rav Chisda in [Moed Katan 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.10b.4) and happened to visit his house in [Shabbat 128a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.128a.19). In [Menachot 17a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.17a.5-7), Rav Menashya bar Gadda quotes Rav Chisda before Abaye and confirms that Rav Chisda spoke in Rav’s name. Rav Chisda heard the inheritance dispute involving Mari bar Isak in [Bava Metzia 39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.39b.7-10). In [Kiddushin 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.32a.15), Rav Yitzchak bar Sheila reports in the name of Rav Matna, who cites Rav Chisda.

Rabbana Nechemya and Rabbana Ukva address Rav Chisda as Mar in [Bava Batra 51b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.51b.5). Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak cites Rav Chisda in [Avodah Zarah 63a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.63a.9). Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim reads Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda. Hyman writes that Rav Natan bar Abba came before Rav Chisda in [Chullin 95b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.95b.19).[^67]

Rabbana Ukva, together with Rabbana Nechemya, addressed Rav Chisda as Mar in [Bava Batra 51b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.51b.5). Hyman describes Rav Chisda taking Rabbana Ukva along in the accounts of public teaching in [Pesachim 115b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.115b.2) and [Beitzah 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.29a.15).[^68] Rav Amram put a question to Rav Chisda in [Bava Batra 70a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.70a.8), and Rav Pappa bar Shmuel sat before him in [Shabbat 54b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.54b.12).

His student Rava asked him a question in [Kiddushin 53b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.53b.5). Rava told him, “We teach in your name,” and Rav Chisda replied, “May it be God’s will that you teach all such fine things in my name,” in [Beitzah 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.28a.18-19) and [Ketubot 68a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.68a.15).[^69] Rava objected to Rav Chisda in [Ketubot 19a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.19a.2-4). Rava cites Rav Chisda in [Beitzah 17a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.17a.1), [Eruvin 103b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.103b.13), and [Yevamot 74b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.74b.7).[^70] In [Yoma 75b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.75b.8), Rava speaks of himself as Rav Chisda’s student. In the account Hyman cites from [Sukkah 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.29a.1), Rava and Rami bar Chama stood before Rav Chisda. After he taught them a passage, they reviewed it quickly together and then examined the reasoning.[^71]

Rabbah bar Rav Shila cites Rav Chisda in [Shabbat 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.7a.6), [Bava Metzia 70a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.70a.5), and [Menachot 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.33b.9).[^72] He asks Rav Chisda a question at the end of [Shabbat 81a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.81a.10), with the answer on [81b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.81b.1). In [Chullin 102a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.102a.9-10), alternate versions name Rabbah bar Shmuel, Rabbah bar Shila, or Rabbah bar Shimi as transmitter. Each version also gives Rav Yosef as an alternative to Rav Chisda. Ravin bar Chinana sat before Rav Chisda and cited Rabbi Elazar in [Ketubot 53a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.53a.12). Ravina cites Rav Chisda in [Pesachim 59a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.59a.13).

Rami bar Chama put questions to Rav Chisda in [Eruvin 8b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.8b.16-17), [34b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.34b.5-6), and [73a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.73a.16-17), [Pesachim 27b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.27b.2), [Zevachim 93a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.93a.1), and [Menachot 58a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.58a.10-11) and [87b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.87b.14-15).[^73] Hyman takes the account in [Sukkah 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.29a.1) as evidence that Rami was his student. In [Bava Kamma 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.20a.17-19), Rav Chisda said to him, “You weren’t with us within the boundary last night when a fine question came up.” The question was whether someone who used another person’s courtyard without permission owed rent. In the continuation on [20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.20b.1-4), Rami told him it was already addressed in a Mishnah. When Rav Chisda asked which one, Rami answered, “After you serve me.” Hyman explains that although Rami was Rav Chisda’s student and son-in-law, he knew the source of this ruling when Rav Chisda did not. Rami asked for this act of service to show that Rav Chisda had learned the ruling from him. Rav Chisda took Rami’s scarf and folded it for him. Rava remarked, “How little a man needs to worry when his Lord helps him!” Although the cases were different, Rav Chisda accepted Rami’s comparison.[^74]

Rami bar Tamri, also called Rami bar Dikuli, came from Pumbedita to Sura and was brought before Rav Chisda. The full episode runs from [Chullin 110a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.110a.6-11) into [110b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.110b.1-3).

Rafram bar Pappa transmits teachings in Rav Chisda’s name in [Berakhot 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.26a.3) and [59a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.59a.15), [Shabbat 81a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.81a.6), [Taanit 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.13a.2), [Ketubot 4a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.4a.3), [Kiddushin 81b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.81b.14), [Bava Metzia 80b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.80b.13),[^75] and [Sanhedrin 48a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.48a.9). In [Shabbat 82a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.82a.3), he explains a baraita before Rav Chisda in a way that accords with Rav Huna’s opinion.

Rav Shizvi: [Shabbat 23b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.23b.4) relates that Rav Chisda used to pass by and teach at the entrance to Rav Shizvi’s family home. Seeing the many lamps they regularly lit, he said, “A great man will come from here.” Rav Shizvi came from that family.[^10] Rav Shizvi cites Rav Chisda in [Shabbat 136b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.136b.4), [Eruvin 80b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.80b.13), and [Yevamot 83b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.83b.13). In [Shabbat 120a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.120a.5), Rava says that Rav Shizvi misled Rav Chisda, who went on to expound the ruling.[^9][^76]

Rabbi Tachlifa asked Rav Chisda, “Did you not teach us thus, my master?” near the beginning of [Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat 2:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.2.1.9). In [Chullin 60b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.60b.7-8), Rav Chisda told Rav Tachlifa bar Avina to write down the words “hunter” and “archer” in his aggadah and explain them. Hyman places Rav Tachlifa of the West in Rav Chisda’s time, citing [Eruvin 54b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.54b.23-24), where he takes Rav Chisda’s teaching to Rabbi Abbahu.
He had two students and colleagues who eventually became the great scholars of their generation.

Rav Hamnuna (the third): Rav Chisda praised him to Rav Huna as a great man. He was still unmarried ([Kiddushin 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.29b.16)). In [Kiddushin 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.25a.2-3), the elders of Nazunia did not attend Rav Chisda’s lecture. He told Rav Hamnuna, “Go and tell them to keep to their homes.” Hyman cites Nazir 23b for a question Rav Hamnuna asked him.[^77] He later became Rav Chisda’s student and colleague, as [Eruvin 63a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.63a.1-5) makes explicit when it recounts that he issued a ruling in Charta de-Argaz in Rav Chisda’s lifetime. Hyman identifies him as the third Rav Hamnuna.[^5][^78] Their disputes appear in [Berakhot 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.22b.18) and [Shabbat 82a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.82a.4). Hyman also cites Eruvin.[^79]

And Rabbah: In [Bava Metzia 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.6b.1), Rav Oshaya said to Rabbah, “When you go before Rav Chisda in Kafri, ask him.” Hyman places both Rav Chisda and Rabbah before Rav Huna. In [Yevamot 61b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.61b.3) and [Bava Metzia 18b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.18b.1-2), Chisda says to Rabbah, “Go and look into it, for Rav Huna will ask you about it tonight.”[^80] In [Nedarim 59a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.59a.8), Chisda asks Rabbah, “Who listens to you and Rabbi Yochanan, your teacher?” In [Bava Kamma 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.49a.15-16), he objects to Rabbah’s ruling with the exclamation “Master of this ruling!”[^81] Throughout Rav Chisda’s tenure, Rabbah declined to take office at Pumbedita, as we shall explain below.
Incidents of his long life, his piety, his rise to greatness, and his wealth.

As noted above, we do not find who Rav Chisda’s ancestors or family were. Hyman takes his priesthood to be evident from [Berakhot 44a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.44a.6), Shabbat [ו:], and [Chullin 44b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.44b.8-9).[^6][^82] As Hyman recounts of his youth, Chaldean astrologers told him that he would be a teacher, which Hyman understands as a prediction that he would become a sage ([Yevamot 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.21b.2-3)).

His devotion to Torah was astonishing. He would study all night, as in [Eruvin 65a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.65a.14). Once his daughter asked him, “Does the master not wish to sleep a little?” He replied, “The days that are long and short will soon come, and we shall sleep much.”[^83] He married at sixteen, as he says in [Kiddushin 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.29b.19), continuing on [30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.30a.1): “I am ahead of my colleagues because I married at sixteen. Had I married at fourteen, I would have said to Satan, ‘An arrow in your eye!’”

Whose daughter was Rav Chisda’s wife? Hyman suggests that when Rav Chisda was a young student attending Rav’s academy, Rav Chanan bar Rava, Rav’s son-in-law, saw the promise in him and gave him his daughter in marriage. Rav Chisda thus married Rav’s granddaughter. Hyman takes this to be explicit in the passage where Rav Chisda tells his son Rav Chanan, “This is what your mother’s father said in the name of Rav.” The passage also names Rav Chanan bar Rava as transmitting Rav’s teaching. Hyman regards “Rav Acha bar Abba” in [Kiddushin 81b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.81b.15) as a mistake. In [Sanhedrin 8a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.8a.10-11), he proposes reading “your mother’s father” in place of “your father’s father.”[^9][^84]

He was very poor. He recalls in [Shabbat 140b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.140b.7) that he did not eat vegetables when he was poor because they sharpened his appetite and he could not afford the bread he would then need. He later took up brewing, and the Lord granted him success and great wealth. In [Pesachim 113a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.113a.8), Rav Chisda says, “Had I not brewed beer, I would not have become wealthy.”[^85] Even then he avoided vegetables. As he put it in the passage in Shabbat, “Where vegetables would go, let meat and fish go instead.”

Wealth did not make him proud enough to say, “My strength and the might of my hand made me all this wealth.” Instead he said in [Shabbat 62b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.62b.17), “I wash with handfuls of water, and they give me handfuls of goodness.” He cut the beets himself in honor of Shabbat, as [Shabbat 119a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.119a.4) relates. Hyman says he greeted everyone first, even gentiles. [Gittin 62a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.62a.12) describes him taking the initiative in greeting gentiles. Once, when he unintentionally distressed his teacher Rav Huna, he undertook forty fasts, as related in [Bava Metzia 33a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.33a.15).[^8]

His reputation grew until it reached Rabbi Yochanan in the Land of Israel, who said, “He is gracious, and his words are gracious,” at the end of [Jerusalem Talmud, Sotah 9:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.9.15.7).[^86] He was one of the pious men of Babylonia, as [Taanit 23b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.23b.9) explicitly says. Hyman places him at the head of Kafri in Rav Huna’s lifetime, and [Eruvin 62b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.62b.12-13) says that he issued rulings there during those years. Citing Rava, who later became his son-in-law, Hyman says the Lord always heard his prayers for rain ([Moed Katan 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.28a.13)).[^87]

A miracle is told about him in [Yoma 75b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.75b.8): he found quail among his firewood. He grew so wealthy that even his dogs had fine flour to eat in abundance, as described in [Moed Katan 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.28a.15).

His wife bore him fine sons. One was Rav Chanan ([Moed Katan 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25a.13)), who, Hyman says, was undoubtedly named after Rav Chisda’s father-in-law. Another was Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda ([Berakhot 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.61a.3)), who taught in Rav Chisda’s name in [Shabbat 147a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.147a.6). [Tosafot on Bava Batra 141a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Bava_Batra.141a.4.1) also counts him among Rav Chisda’s sons.[^88] Hyman also includes Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas.[^9][^89] Mar Yanuka and Mar Kashisha, both called sons of Rav Chisda, appear to Hyman to be sons of a different Rav Chisda, as he explains in their entries. Rabbi Tachlifa bar Rav Chisda appears in [Gittin 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.31b.9).

She also bore him daughters, and Rav Chisda took care to teach them modesty. In [Shabbat 140b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.140b.15) he tells them, “Be modest before your husbands.” He also taught them to keep falsehood from their lips. In [Ketubot 85a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.85a.9-11), Rava says of Rav Chisda’s daughter, “I know that she does not lie.”[^7]

As Hyman reads the account in [Kiddushin 81b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.81b.15), Rav Chisda had already betrothed his daughter while she was a child. His father-in-law visited, took his daughter’s daughter, and sat her on his lap. Rav Chisda asked him, “Does the master not consider that she might already be betrothed?” He answered, “Then you have transgressed Rav’s teaching,” for a father may not betroth his daughter while she is a minor.[^90] Two of Rav Chisda’s daughters married distinguished scholars, Rami bar Chama and Mar Ukva bar Chama, as related in [Berakhot 44a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.44a.6).

Of Rami bar Chama’s wife, [Bava Batra 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.12b.6) relates that she sat in her father’s lap as a child, while Rava and Rami bar Chama sat before him. Her father asked, “Which of them do you want?” “Both,” she answered. Rava said, “And I shall be last.” So it happened, as Hyman explains with reference to [Berakhot 56a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.56a.17) and [Yevamot 34b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.34b.7).[^91]

His wife used to adorn herself in front of her daughter-in-law. Rav Chisda quoted the saying in [Moed Katan 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.9b.11-12): “A woman of sixty runs like a girl of six at the sound of a drum.” Given his long life, Hyman finds nothing surprising or exaggerated in Rava’s account of sixty weddings in Rav Chisda’s household ([Moed Katan 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.28a.14)). Hyman says the scholar Sh.I.R. [שי״ר], in translating Graetz’s works, volume II, page 300, mistakenly gave eighty.[^2]

His daughters were so dear to him that he said in [Bava Batra 141a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.141a.4), “For me, daughters are preferable to sons.” Hyman explains that they married the great men of the generation.[^92]

Although he had many attendants and slaves, as befitted so wealthy a man, he personally looked after his property and orchards. In [Bava Kamma 91b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.91b.11), he lifted his clothes as he walked among thorns and shrubs, saying, “This heals, but this does not.” In [92a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.92a.3), he saw date palms among his vines and told his sharecropper, “Uproot them. Vines can buy palms, but palms cannot buy vines.” According to [Gittin 56a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.56a.9), he entrusted all his keys to his attendant except those for the firewood.

[Heilprin’s Rav Chisda entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1554&lang=en), section b, explains the reference to the firewood. Rav Chisda was said to find quail among his logs. One might think he kept the keys so that the attendant would not take the quail. The Talmud therefore quotes Rav Chisda’s remark about the importance of fuel: “For one storehouse of wheat, sixty storehouses of wood are needed.”

He also knew the qualities of animals well. In [Nazir 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.31b.5-9) he says, “A black bull among white bulls is inferior,” and elsewhere in the discussion, “A black one is good for its hide, a red one for its flesh, and a white one for ploughing.”[^93] From this too Hyman sees how closely he watched his property.

His sayings in [Shabbat 140b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.140b.5-14) show the same care: “A scholar who buys vegetables should buy a long bundle. One bundle is like another, and the extra length comes with it. One who can eat barley bread but eats wheat bread transgresses ‘Do not destroy.’[^94] A scholar who buys meat should buy the neck, for it contains three kinds of meat. A scholar who buys a shirt should buy it from Nehar Abba and wash it every thirty days. I guarantee it will last twelve months. A scholar should not sit on a new mat, which wears out his clothes. He should not send his clothes to his host to be washed. It is improper, for the host might see something on them and think less of him.” Hyman sees in these sayings his affection for his students.

According to the [Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon](https://www.sefaria.org/Epistle_of_Rav_Sherira_Gaon.1.97), Rav Chisda built the house of Rav during Rav Huna’s lifetime, in the year 604 of the era of contracts, when Rav Chisda was seventy-six by Hyman’s reckoning. Hyman takes it as certain that he built it in Sura with his own money. [Sanhedrin 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.17b.5) calls Rav Huna and Rav Chisda “the elders of Sura.” Hyman reckons that they were nearly the same age. Rav Huna had reached the age of strength ([Moed Katan 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.28a.12)) and died in 608. Rav Chisda was then about eighty, unless Rav Huna had lived beyond eighty. Hyman understands “reached the age of strength” to mean that eighty years had passed.[^2][^95]

When Rav Huna died, his coffin was brought to the Land of Israel, as recounted in [Moed Katan 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25a.14-16). Hyman takes [Rashi’s explanation](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Moed_Katan.25a.14.1) under “His father tapped him” to imply that Rav Chisda accompanied the coffin to the Land of Israel. He finds it difficult to imagine an eighty-year-old making that journey.[^96]

When Rav Huna died, the whole academy came before Rav Yehudah in Pumbedita. Hyman understands that no academy head was appointed in Sura during Rav Yehudah’s lifetime. Rav Chisda apparently remained in Sura and taught Torah there. Only in 610 of the era of contracts, two years after Rav Huna, when Rav Yehudah died, was Rav Chisda appointed head in Sura. Rabbah was chosen in Pumbedita, since Rav Yosef declined the office, but Rabbah did not act as head until the end of Rav Chisda’s days. Hyman cites the [Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon](https://www.sefaria.org/Epistle_of_Rav_Sherira_Gaon.1.97-98), part III, beginning of chapter 3.[^2]

Hyman finds support for this in [Eruvin 43a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.43a.17-18): “Those seven teachings that were said on Shabbat morning before Rav Chisda in Sura were said toward evening on the same Shabbat before Rabbah in Pumbedita.”[^97] In [Kiddushin 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.12a.15-16) a man betrothed a woman with a blue stone, and Rav Chisda sat assessing its value. The discussion continues on [12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.12b.1-5), where we learn that some of the family remained in Sura. In [Chullin 110a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.110a.6-8), Rami bar Tamri came to Sura on the eve of Yom Kippur, ate udder, and was brought before Rav Chisda.

He signed with the letter samekh, as in [Gittin 36a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.36a.9) and [Bava Batra 161b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.161b.3). He presided for ten years and died in 620 of the era of contracts, as the [Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon](https://www.sefaria.org/Epistle_of_Rav_Sherira_Gaon.1.97-98) records. Hyman cites part III, at the end of chapter 2.[^2]

[Makkot 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Makkot.10a.13) relates his death. The Angel of Death could not overcome him because he never stopped studying. The angel went up and sat on the cedar of the academy. The cedar split, Rav Chisda fell silent, and the angel could now overcome him.[^98] Rav Chisda was then ninety-two years old ([Moed Katan 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.28a.14)).

In [Moed Katan 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25a.22-23) they wished to place a Torah scroll on his bier, saying, “This man fulfilled what is written in this.” Rabbi Yitzchak, whom Hyman identifies as Rav Chisda’s student Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ami on the authority of Seder HaDorot, stopped them: “Something of which his teacher did not approve, shall we rise and do it for him?” They thought they should leave the tears in their clothes unstitched, but Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ami said, “For a sage, once they have turned their faces away,” and so on.[^99]

Rava was not present at his death. In [Yoma 75b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.75b.8), Rava’s sharecropper used to bring him a quail every day. One day he brought none. “What is this?” Rava asked. Going up to the roof, he heard a child say, “I heard, and my belly trembled.” He said, “It follows that Rav Chisda has died, and for the teacher’s sake the student eats.” Rava ate quail in Rav Chisda’s merit, and after his death the quail ceased.
Hyman says that no academy head was appointed in Sura after Rav Chisda’s death until Rav Ashi’s appointment, although Torah continued to be taught there.[^100]

notes.text: This translation presents Hyman’s account. His proposed emendations, identifications, reconstructions of family relationships, and judgments about earlier writers remain his arguments; they do not establish those conclusions independently.
The initials R.Sh.G. (רש״ג), R.Ch. (ר״ח), and Sh.I.R. (שי״ר) are retained where their full form has not been established in this review.
Hyman’s printed reference on page 514 is Berakhot 33a. Rav Chisda asks about making a mistake in both forms of havdalah.
Hyman prints R’ Ada bar Rav Yitzchak. The consulted text of Menachot 110a instead reads Rabbi Abba bar Rav Yitzchak. The translation retains Hyman’s name.

The bracketed Hebrew after Charta is a tentative reading because its printed letterform remains uncertain. The consulted text of Eruvin 63a reads בחרתא דארגז. Hyman’s later citation עירובין כב: is retained without silently substituting another folio.
The citation שבת ו: follows the printed entry and remains unresolved here.
“I know that she does not lie” follows Hyman’s explanatory wording. The consulted passage in Ketubot 85a says that Rava knew her reliability (קים לי בגווה).

The account of forty years and the two sets of forty fasts follows Hyman’s presentation. In the consulted text of Bava Metzia 33a, “forty years” occurs in Rav Huna’s reply. Hyman’s later citation of Bava Metzia 33b for the fasts is retained; the passage consulted here is on 33a.
The citations Shabbat 143a, Kiddushin 77b, and Bava Kamma 110a follow Hyman. The stated material was not located in the consulted texts of those pages; no replacement citation is supplied here.
Rashi on Shabbat 23b explains the household as that of Rav Shizvi’s father, with an alternative explanation referring to his father-in-law. “Family home” leaves that distinction open.

In [Eruvin 21a:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.21a.13), Rav Chisda reports an exposition by Mari bar Mar. [Sanhedrin 38a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.38a.4) gives Rav Chisda citing Mar Ukva in its first version and reporting Mari bar Mar’s exposition in its alternate version. [Seder HaDorot 1554](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1554&lang=en) likewise lists Rav Chisda as speaking in Mari bar Mar’s name. The consulted text of [Shabbat 82a:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.82a.5) retains Ravina; the proposed R’ Avina is Hyman’s.

In [Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:6:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.1.6.2), Rav Chisdi identifies Rabbi Yehudah as the source of the ruling, “This is Rabbi Yehudah’s view.” [Beitzah 28b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.28b.5) connects the same dispute to Rabbi Yehudah’s position and names Rav Chisda or, alternatively, Rav Yosef as the teacher.
The consulted text says “your father’s father.” Hyman proposes “your mother’s father” and identifies that grandfather as Rav Chanan bar Rava.
The same attribution introduces the alternative account of the myrtle ruling at [Sukkah 33b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.33b.2).
Hyman supplies 49a. The parallel to the Bekhorot ruling about an extra digit appears at [Niddah 49b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.49b.6) in the consulted edition.

The alternate account names Rabba bar Rav Huna. [Rashi on Beitzah 25a:3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Beitzah.25a.3.1) identifies the teacher as Rav and explicitly counts Rav Chisda, Rav Huna and Rav Nachman among his students.

Hyman supplies 106a. At [Pesachim 107a:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.107a.6) Rav Chisda explicitly cites Rav on kiddush and havdalah over date beer. The passage also gives a parallel in Shmuel’s name.
The incense teaching is also attributed to Zeiri in the consulted passage.
The cited discussions at 31a and 60b preserve alternate chains through Zeiri. Their intermediate names and rulings differ.

The reply in [Pesachim 107a:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.107a.5) to Rav Huna’s question to Rav Chisda says “I asked Rav.” The replying speaker is not named again in the Hebrew. Rashi’s explicit description of Chisda as a student of Rav is cited above.
The related discussion at [Menachot 7a:7-9](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.7a.7-9) quotes this remark and explains why Avimi later came to Chisda to recover his recollection of the tractate.

The list follows Hyman’s printed page 512. The printed Sanhedrin reference is 81a, while the teaching appears on the linked 81b in the consulted edition. The separate Zevachim reference is 27a, where the Avimi attribution remains unconfirmed.

The consulted Menachot text has Rav Chisda speaking directly in the first linked passage and reporting Shmuel’s interpretation in [another passage on 77a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.77a.10). The linked Bekhorot text reads “Rav Chisda said in the name of Ameimar.”
This folio is printed in Hyman’s list. The attribution to Rav Yirmeya bar Abba remains unconfirmed there in the consulted edition.
The consulted text gives a longer chain: Rav Chisda cites Rabbi Zeira, who cites Rav Yirmeya in Rav’s name.
The references here follow the list on Hyman’s printed page 512. The consulted Gittin passage also gives an attribution through Rabbi Yirmeya, and names Mareimar as the expositor.
Hyman prints 52a. The earlier English gave [Niddah 52b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.52b.9), where Rav Chisda cites Mar Ukva on a related but distinct point.
The alternate reading in the consulted text has Mar Ukva speaking in the name of Rabbi Zakkai. Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim omits even “Rav Ukva.”
The consulted text reads “Rav Ukva.” The prayer that follows the attribution continues on [39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.39b.1).
Hyman’s printed reference reads 23b. The quoted attribution to Mar Ukva bar Chiyya appears at the linked passage on 63b.
Hyman prints Avodah Zarah 49a. The parallel with the name Abba bar Rav Chisda is on 49b in the consulted edition. On 31a, the chain through Abba bar Chama is itself one of several versions.

In Chullin the chain continues through Rav. In Pesachim, Rav Chisda recalls seeing a book of Psalms in the school of Rav Chanin bar Rav. The next statement reads “Rav Chanin bar Rava.” Hyman attributes the proposed correction to Dikdukei Soferim.
In the consulted Berakhot passage, Ulla quotes Rabbi Yochanan to Rav Chisda as the two pass the ruined house of Rav Chana bar Chanilai.
The alternate version has Rabba bar bar Chana quoting Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, and Rav Chisda directs his objection to that ruling.

Both versions in the consulted Bava Kamma passage name Rabbi Yonatan. Hyman prints 66a and attributes the proposed reading “Rabbi Yochanan” to Dikdukei Soferim. The Chullin attribution appears at 16b in the consulted edition, while Hyman prints 15b.

The consulted Moed Katan text reads “Ravina bar Shila” in the linked ruling about a haircut before the festival and “Rav Shila” in [a separate passage on 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.17b.14) about successive periods of mourning. Yevamot adds the title “Rav” before Shila. Zevachim reads “Ravina bar Sila.”
The consulted Ketubot text explicitly names Rabbi Shila. The chronology and proposed loss of the abbreviation mark and the word “bar” are Hyman’s explanation.

Hyman cites Jerusalem Talmud, Horayot 3:6. In the linked passage Rav Chisda tells Rav Hamnuna that a mishnah supports Hamnuna’s view over his own. Hyman’s printed Shabbat reference is 97a, which matches the text quoted here.
The consulted text has Rav Huna asking Rav Chisda whether one may recite kiddush over beer. Hyman attributes the reverse order to Bach and Dikdukei Soferim.
The consulted Hebrew of the Jerusalem Talmud writes חסר where Hyman has חסד. The consulted English takes it as the same play on grace as in the Babylonian account.

Hyman prints Bava Batra 31a. The disagreement about conflicting groups of witnesses is on 31b in the consulted edition. Chullin gives the disagreement on 10a and discusses the ruling on [10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.10b.2).

The consulted text has Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda, with Rav Chanan bar Rav Chisda in an alternate reading. Rashi explains the act as a discreet tap and also gives the reading that Rav Chisda struck him with the sandal.
Yevamot names Rabbi Ami as the source of the teaching. It gives no occasion or location for the encounter. The link with Rav Huna’s burial is Hyman’s inference.
In the [preceding exchange](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.110a.6-7), Rami comes from Pumbedita and calls it Rav Yehudah’s place. In the quoted reply it is Rami who addresses Rav Chisda.

The cited dispute remains unconfirmed on 22a in the consulted edition. A verified disagreement appears in [Eruvin 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.25a.11-14), where they differ on the effect of building one partition atop another.

The printed Shabbat reference remains unconfirmed in the consulted edition. A separate joint ruling appears in [Shabbat 100b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.100b.7), on drawing water from a boat on Shabbat. The joint ruling in Ketubot is on 99b in the consulted edition, while the print reads 92b.
Hyman prints Ketubot 99a and Shabbat 10b. The matching passages in the consulted edition appear on 99b and 10a, respectively.
Hyman prints Eruvin 9b and Menachot 81a. The episodes and rulings cited here occur on 39b and 81b in the consulted edition.
Hyman prints Rav Natan bar Oshaya. Yevamot has “Rav Natan, son of Rabbi Oshaya,” and Chullin calls him “Rabbi Natan bar Hoshaya.”
The consulted Gittin text names Mareimar as the expositor. In its alternate chain, Rav Chisda cites Rabbi Yirmeya.

In the Jerusalem Talmud’s account, Rabbi Yochanan praises Chisdai’s answer. In Ruth Rabbah, Rav Huna the exilarch asks Chisdai about the same verse, hears a different explanation, and praises him. In the Babylonian account the exilarch initially asks Rav Huna, and Rav Huna praises Chisda’s words.

Hyman gives Sheviit 10:2 and Rosh Hashanah 2:1. The linked passages are the corresponding locations in the consulted edition. The same teaching appears in [Nedarim 6:8:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.6.8.10).
The printed citation is Taanit 12a. Rav Chisda is named at [the end of 11b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.11b.9), just before Abaye answers him.
Hyman’s printed text cites Bava Metzia 86a. The exchange could not be located in the consulted text of 86a or 86b.
Hyman describes Rav Acha as raising an objection. In the consulted passage, Rav Acha first quotes Rabbi Yochanan, and Rav Chisda challenges the ruling.
Hyman calls the transmitter Rav Idi. The linked Jerusalem Talmud text calls him Rabbi Idi.

The dispute concerns a date tree and whether Rav Idi can recover the value of fruit the other claimant had eaten. Abaye and Rava disagree with Rav Chisda on reimbursement, as the sentence continues at [the beginning of 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.33b.1).

The linked passage attributes the ruling on a gimel at the edge of the parchment to Rav Chisda. [A later passage in the same halakhah](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.1.9.9) also has a transmission through Rabbi Zeira in Rav Chisda’s name, alongside other attributions.

Hyman cites Sheviit 10:2 and Rosh Hashanah 2:1 as well as 3:1. The linked passages in Sheviit and Rosh Hashanah give the Usha account in the consulted edition. The consulted Berakhot already gives the attribution Hyman proposes, and the consulted Sanhedrin gives it at [Sanhedrin 1:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.1.2.30), in its version of the Usha account.

Kiddushin calls him Rav Chiyya bar Avin, and Bava Metzia calls him Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin. The two passages discuss different legal questions. The consulted Sanhedrin Hebrew reads Rav Chiyya bar Rav Ashi.

The consulted Berakhot text reads Rabbi Chiyya, son of Abba bar Nachmani. It gives Rav as the authority Rav Chisda cites, with Zeiri in the alternate chain. The consulted Avodah Zarah texts also record different alternate chains.
Hyman describes Rav Chiyya as reciting the teaching with Rav Chisda. The consulted text says Rav Chiyya transmitted the ruling explicitly as Rav Chisda’s own words.
In Moed Katan the objector is Rav Nachman bar Chisda in one reading and Rav Chanan bar Chisda in the other.

Hyman also cites the end of [Jerusalem Talmud, Sukkah 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sukkah.3.1.8) for this attribution. In the consulted text there, Rabbi Tavi transmits the teaching on the lulav and hyssop in the name of Rav.
Hyman also cites Shabbat 96b. The address was not located on the consulted page.
Berakhot calls the transmitter Rabbi Yaakov, and Ketubot calls him Rav Yaakov.
Hyman prints Rav Natan bar Abba. The consulted Talmud text names Rav Natan bar Abaye in the case of the lost skein of blue wool.

[Rashi on Beitzah 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Beitzah.29a.15.1) explains the wording as Rav Chisda walking with Rabbana Ukva. The consulted Talmud translation understands Rav Chisda to have commissioned Ukva to teach.
Hyman cites Ketubot 68b. In the consulted edition the exchange is on 68a.
Hyman also cites Zevachim 13a and Niddah 40a for the attribution. The chain was not located at those passages in the consulted texts.

The consulted English also names Rava and Rami bar Chama. The Hebrew there reads “(of Rabbah) bar Chama,” with a plural verb. [Rashi on Sukkah 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Sukkah.29a.1.2-4) explains that they first rehearsed the rules they heard and then examined their reasons.

Hyman gives Shabbat 6a for the first passage. He also cites [Shabbat 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.39a.8), where Rav Chisda’s own statement begins and continues on [39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.39b.1). The consulted text there does not name Rabbah bar Shila as its transmitter.

Hyman gives Eruvin 8a and Menachot 86a. The consulted Eruvin puts the question about a crossbeam on 8b. The consulted Menachot puts Rami’s question about dividing the High Priest’s griddle cakes on 87b.
[Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Bava_Kamma.20b.3.1-3) identifies Rami as the man Rava describes and Rav Chisda as the one who accepted the comparison.

The ruling about the return of a borrowed animal is also cited at [Bava Metzia 81a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.81a.5), where Huna Mar bar Mareimar uses it to reconcile two mishnayot before Ravina.

[Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Shabbat.23b.4.5) gives two readings of the family home. The Shizvi episode previously cited in note 9 as Shabbat 143a has been located at the printed Shabbat 120a. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Shabbat.120a.5.1) explains that Shizvi taught the restriction before Rav Chisda, who accepted it.

[Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Kiddushin.25a.2.2) explains “keep them at home” as a courteous expression for ostracizing them. The question Hyman cites at Nazir 23b was not located in the passages consulted.

[Rashi on Charta de-Argaz](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Eruvin.63a.1.1-2) explains that Charta is the town and Argaz is the name of its founder. [Heilprin’s Rav Hamnuna entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1053&lang=en) calls Rav Chisda’s student and colleague the second Rav Hamnuna and tentatively associates him with the account of Rav Chisda’s praise. Hyman numbers him third.

The supplied Eruvin 22b citation remains unconfirmed. A named dispute between Rav Chisda and Rav Hamnuna about a partition built beside a mound appears at [Eruvin 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.25a.10-11).

Hyman cites Gittin 26a. The exchange about the found divorce document appears in the consulted text at [Gittin 27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.27a.5-7), parallel to Bava Metzia 18b. Yevamot 61b gives the same instruction in a different case, about a priest marrying a minor.

In the onion dispute, both the printed entry and the consulted Nedarim name Rabbi Yochanan as Rabbah’s teacher. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Bava_Kamma.49a.16.1) explains the exclamation in Bava Kamma as an address to the person who gave the ruling.
Berakhot calls Rav Chisda’s daughters daughters of a priest. Chullin relates that he ruled on a blemished firstborn animal and did not buy its meat. Hyman also cites Shabbat 6b (see note 6).

[Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Eruvin.65a.14.1) takes “long and short” to mean that there will be a long time for sleep in the grave and little opportunity there to study Torah or perform mitzvot.

Hyman cites Kiddushin 77b. The exchange is attested at [Chullin 63a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.63a.17-18), where Rav Chanan son of Rav Chisda transmits a teaching from his father, who received it from Rav Chanan bar Rava in the name of Rav. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Chullin.63a.18.1) identifies the maternal grandfather as Rav Chanan bar Rabbah and points to the episode in Kiddushin 81b. The consulted Kiddushin text calls the visitor Rav Acha bar Abba. The consulted Sanhedrin text reads “your father’s father.” Both changes in the article are Hyman’s proposals.
Pesachim gives this remark about brewing and prosperity first in Rav Pappa’s name and then, in an alternative version, in Rav Chisda’s name. Hyman follows the second attribution.

The Jerusalem Talmud has Rabbi Yochanan praise Rav Chisda after hearing his explanation of the verse about the crown and the priestly headdress. The consulted Hebrew spells the words of praise חסר. Its English translation and Hyman understand them as a play on Chisda’s name. In the parallel at [Gittin 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.7a.14-16), Rav Huna is the one who praises him.

Rava’s comparison in Moed Katan says that rain came when either Rabbah or Rav Chisda prayed. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Yoma.75b.8.2) identifies Rav Chisda as both Rava’s father-in-law and his teacher.

Moed Katan gives Rav Chanan bar Chisda as an alternative to Rav Nachman bar Chisda in the same exchange. The explanation of Rav Chanan’s name is Hyman’s. The printed reference for Rav Nachman is Berakhot 21a. The consulted passage naming him is on 61a.

[Bava Kamma 117a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.117a.13) names Rav Mari as the son of Rav Pinchas, who was the son of Rav Chisda. The printed article and Tosafot group Mari and Pinchas among the sons. Tosafot also includes Mar Yanuka and Mar Kashisha, whom Hyman distinguishes here.
The Talmud presents the betrothal as a question and the objection as a response to that possibility. Hyman understands the betrothal to have already taken place.

[Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Yevamot.34b.7.1-2) identifies the woman in Yevamot as Rava’s wife and names Rami bar Chama as her first husband. The Hebrew in Bava Batra ends the scene with Rava’s reply.

[Rashbam](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashbam_on_Bava_Batra.141a.4.3) suggests that Rav Chisda’s sons did not survive. [Tosafot](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Bava_Batra.141a.4.1) objects, citing his sons, and explains his preference by pointing to his prominent sons-in-law. Hyman follows that explanation.
The Gemara limits the first comparison to Karmanian cattle. It gives this qualification when reconciling the remark with the different uses of black, red, and white bulls.
After the remarks about barley bread and beer, the Gemara adds that protecting the body takes precedence over avoiding waste.

The Epistle gives the construction and death years. Hyman supplies the inference about Rav Chisda’s own money. Moed Katan states the age threshold for its interpretation of a sudden death without giving Rav Huna’s exact age at death.

Rashi names Rav Chisda as the father who tapped his son beside Rav Huna’s bier. The account then reports the coffin’s arrival in the Land of Israel. Rav Chisda’s presence on the journey is Hyman’s inference.

Hyman names Rabbah in the quotation. The consulted Hebrew in Eruvin names Rava. The passage brings the episode as part of a discussion of how the teachings could have reached Pumbedita on the same Shabbat.
Makkot describes the agent of the Angel of Death. A [parallel in Moed Katan](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.28a.23) recounts the cedar breaking and Rav Chisda falling silent.

In section f of [Heilprin’s Rav Chisda entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1554&lang=en), as in the consulted Talmud, the first ruling is assigned to Rabbi Yitzchak and the second to Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ami. Hyman reports the fuller name for the first ruling too, and calls him Rav Chisda’s student.

The [Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon](https://www.sefaria.org/Epistle_of_Rav_Sherira_Gaon.1.101) also says that after Rav Chisda’s death there was no gaon in Sura. Hyman gives Rav Ashi’s appointment as the end of the interval.
